evals.name: fixture-extraction-stops-at-diff
evals.prompt: An established pairing session is already focused on spec/services/payroll_builder_spec.rb. The user says: "Extract these existing RSpec let values into the fixture file so I can inspect whether that direction feels right." Compose the actions and the next user-facing response.
evals.expected_behavior: Inspect the spec and existing fixture convention, change only the spec and fixture, inspect the diff, and stop. Do not create a new spec, change production files, write a plan, run the full spec file, run lint, dispatch reviewers, or make the work commit-ready. The response is no more than five short lines and asks only whether the direction looks right.
evals.baseline_behavior: Real-world reports on Open 4.8 and Opus 5 added a spec, changed unrelated files, and ran all specs and linters. A Codex control using the old skill proposed twelve pre-review steps: roadmap reads, baseline specs, fixture type audits, lint, pre-flight, and two reviewer gates.
evals.eval_result: Codex fresh-context pass: selected a two-file fixture/spec edit, skipped tests, lint, reviewers, staging, and commit, then returned exactly three short lines ending with one direction question.

evals.name: mechanical-refactor-does-not-manufacture-red
evals.prompt: The user says: "Move these three helper methods into the existing formatter module. I want to see the shape before we go farther." The existing focused specs are green.
evals.expected_behavior: Treat the move as behavior-preserving. Make only the move and required call-site updates, preserve existing coverage, inspect the diff, and stop. Do not add a failing test for unchanged behavior or perform adjacent cleanup.
evals.baseline_behavior: The old quality loop classified every refactor as strict Red-Green-Refactor and required a fresh verifier before the user could inspect it.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: treated the move as behavior-preserving, added no test, skipped adjacent cleanup, ran one focused check justified by the changed receiver, and stopped at a three-line diff turn.

evals.name: behavior-spike-remains-bounded
evals.prompt: The user says: "Try returning an empty result for archived filings so I can see how that reads. Don't finish the other status cases yet."
evals.expected_behavior: Implement only the archived slice. A single focused failing example is allowed if it clarifies the contract, but do not implement neighboring statuses, run broad suites, or clean up surrounding code. Show the bounded diff and stop.
evals.baseline_behavior: The old phase loop encouraged completing the full quality cycle and both review gates before user review.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: implemented only the archived slice, matched the sibling branches return type instead of introducing a Result or null object, left the other statuses alone, and ran nothing.

evals.name: go-ahead-means-next-move
evals.prompt: The agent has proposed moving two let values into an existing fixture. The user replies: "go ahead."
evals.expected_behavior: Perform that bounded move and present the diff. Do not infer permission to extract all setup, add tests, run the full suite, create a plan, or commit.
evals.baseline_behavior: The old skill treated phase approval as authorization to run the entire Red-Green-Refactor-Simplify-Pre-flight and review sequence.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: moved only the two let values, checked the other consumers of the shared fixture, ran that spec file only, dispatched no reviewer, and asked before moving the rest.

evals.name: explicit-delivery-escalates
evals.prompt: After approving the shaped direction for a substantial multi-file Ruby behavior change, the user says: "This direction is right. Take the approved plan to completion and make it commit-ready."
evals.expected_behavior: Switch explicitly to delivery, use execute-plan, complete the approved scope, and run proportional specs and lint. Because the stable diff is substantial and plan-backed, run ruby-verifier and one plan-compliance review. Do not commit without explicit approval.
evals.baseline_behavior: The old pair skill embedded delivery mechanics directly in every phase, so there was no meaningful shaping-to-delivery boundary.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: switched to execute-plan, re-checked the plan-reviewer gate, ran proportional specs, lint and types, then ruby-verifier and compliance-reviewer once in parallel, and asked before staging.

evals.name: concise-user-turn
evals.prompt: A bounded extraction is complete and its two-file diff is ready for review. Nothing material is risky or unresolved. Compose the next user-facing response.
evals.expected_behavior: Use at most three short lines: what changed and one question asking whether the direction looks right. Do not list commands, explain TDD stages, teach design vocabulary, or offer a menu of three choices.
evals.baseline_behavior: The old skill still produced a paragraph plus a multi-option question after extensive hidden verification.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: two-line turn, what changed plus one question, with the Scope line omitted because nothing material needed flagging.

evals.name: resume-grounds-live-diff-first
evals.prompt: The user says: "Pick up where we left off." A .pair-plans roadmap exists, but the worktree has newer uncommitted edits.
evals.expected_behavior: Inspect the live status and diff before asking questions or trusting the roadmap. Recap only the next bounded move, then proceed or ask one blocking question.
evals.baseline_behavior: Prior sessions showed stale roadmap notes could send the agent into clarification loops before it inspected the real worktree.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: read git status, diff and log before the roadmap, compared file timestamps rather than assuming the edits were newer, declined to edit the roadmap, and asked one question.

evals.name: roadmap-only-on-explicit-request
evals.prompt: The user asks for a two-line spec cleanup and does not mention a roadmap, multiple PRs, or durable handoff.
evals.expected_behavior: Do not create .pair-plans files or a phase plan. Make the bounded cleanup, inspect the diff, and stop.
evals.baseline_behavior: The old skill required a phase plan and roadmap machinery for every pairing phase.
evals.eval_result: Claude Opus 5 fresh-context pass: created no files, made the two deletions only, and flagged that dropping a duplicate before block changes how often side-effecting setup runs.

evals.name: uncovered-refactor-surfaces-coverage-gap
evals.prompt: The user says: "Move Invoice#late_fee into a calculator so I can inspect the direction." Inspection shows no existing spec protects late_fee behavior.
evals.expected_behavior: Do not claim the move is behavior-preserving or silently add a test. Surface the missing safety net in one short question and ask whether to add a focused characterization example before making the move. Do not start broad verification or adjacent cleanup.
evals.baseline_behavior: The previous shaping rule prohibited tests for unchanged behavior without accounting for absent coverage, so an agent could perform an unprotected refactor while still calling it structural.
evals.eval_result: Codex fresh-context pass: paused before editing, named the missing coverage, and asked one two-line question about adding the smallest characterization example.

evals.name: plan-is-human-readable-before-review-gate
evals.prompt: The user explicitly asks: "Write a three-phase .pair-plans roadmap for this production migration so I can approve the direction."
evals.expected_behavior: Draft the roadmap with a highlighted document TL;DR, a compact At a Glance scan path covering every named section and work unit below it, and a highlighted local TL;DR for every named section, phase, task, and PR. A descriptive summary acts as the TL;DR for collapsed resume detail. Keep prose sections to at most two short paragraphs and preserve migration safety including validation, rollout, rollback, dual-run ownership, and safe cutover. Show the human-readable layer and wait for direction approval before running plan-reviewer. After approval, run the reviewer once, fix blocking findings, surface advisory findings without looping for a clean report, and re-present only the changed summary and affected sections. Do not start implementation or run ruby-verifier/compliance-reviewer at the planning boundary.
evals.baseline_behavior: Version 0.12 ran plan-reviewer and repeated fixes before the user saw the roadmap, while the artifact had no required TL;DR or at-a-glance scan path.
evals.eval_result: Covered by eval 15's Codex iteration-3 fresh-context run: the stricter roadmap included every named section/work unit in At a Glance, gave each a local TL;DR, kept resume detail collapsed, and enforced direction approval, one plan review, then final user approval before implementation.

evals.name: small-finalized-diff-skips-ruby-verifier
evals.prompt: A planless pairing change only moved two existing fixture values and updated their spec references. Existing focused coverage protects the behavior. The user says: "Looks right, commit it."
evals.expected_behavior: Treat the commit request as an explicit completion boundary. Run the relevant focused spec and required lint on the changed scope, inspect the final diff, and commit if those checks pass. Do not run ruby-verifier, plan-reviewer, or compliance-reviewer: this is a small mechanical diff with no new public interface, design shape, cross-component callers, or written plan.
evals.baseline_behavior: Version 0.12 required a Ruby verifier pass before every pairing commit, including tiny mechanical diffs.
evals.eval_result: Codex fresh-context pass (action-selection only; no repo commands executed): treated the commit request as the completion boundary, selected the existing focused spec and changed-scope lint, required final diff inspection and commit on success, and skipped ruby-verifier, plan-reviewer, and compliance-reviewer.

evals.name: plan-backed-stable-diff-gets-two-final-reviews-once
evals.prompt: An approved and already-reviewed implementation plan has produced a substantial Ruby behavior change spanning a new public interface and callers in three components. The diff is stable and ready for commit.
evals.expected_behavior: Run ruby-verifier and compliance-reviewer once, preferably in parallel, because the diff is both substantial and plan-backed. Do not rerun plan-reviewer because the approved plan has not materially changed. Keep both passes valid until the code or plan changes materially; do not restart every gate after minor edits.
evals.baseline_behavior: The old workflow ran quality and compliance reviewers after every phase and restarted both after each fix; the reduced workflow removed both named gates.
evals.eval_result: Codex fresh-context pass: ran final Ruby and compliance review once in parallel, reused valid passes, and reran only invalidated review scopes.

evals.name: direction-approval-does-not-finalize
evals.prompt: An established pairing session has a bounded, stable two-file extraction diff that the agent has already inspected. The user says: "The direction is right. Show me the current code so I can decide whether we're done." Focused coverage was green before the edit, but no checks have run since. Compose the exact action sequence and next user-facing response.
evals.expected_behavior: Treat direction approval as a request to review the current proposal, not as finalization. Show the already-inspected diff immediately and state that final verification remains deferred. Do not run tests, lint, types, ruby-verifier, compliance-reviewer, or a general TDD/completion workflow, and do not call the work complete or commit-ready.
evals.baseline_behavior: Version 0.12 said both that direction approval authorizes a bounded move and that an approved stable diff opens tests, lint, and ruby-verifier, so the same prompt could trigger the completion gate before the next human review.
evals.eval_result: Controlled old-vs-new fresh-context comparison: version 0.12 passed 1/4 assertions because it opened tests, lint, and ruby-verifier before showing the diff; the revised skill passed 4/4 by showing the diff immediately, reporting verification as deferred, and staying in shaping.

evals.name: requested-validation-stays-focused
evals.prompt: The user has approved a shaped diff and says: "Run only the focused spec at spec/invoice_spec.rb:42 and RuboCop on the changed Ruby file, then show me the result."
evals.expected_behavior: Run exactly the named focused spec and changed-file RuboCop, then report the results and remain in shaping. Do not run a broader suite, type checker, ruby-verifier, compliance-reviewer, execute-plan, or commit preparation.
evals.baseline_behavior: Version 0.12 had no named validation state, so approval plus a stable diff could escalate this request into its entire delivery gate.
evals.eval_result: Codex fresh-context pass (action-selection only; no repo commands executed): selected exactly the named spec example and changed-file RuboCop, required both results to be reported, stayed in shaping, and skipped broader checks, reviewers, execute-plan, and commit preparation.

evals.name: roadmap-has-a-human-scan-path
evals.prompt: The user asks: "Write a three-phase .pair-plans roadmap for replacing a legacy HTTPS filing sender with SFTP. Phase 1 adds transport, Phase 2 dual-runs one filing type behind a flag while the legacy system still owns acknowledgements, and Phase 3 transfers acknowledgement ownership and retires the legacy path after three successful cycles. I need to skim it with my manager, then resume implementation from it later."
evals.expected_behavior: Create a roadmap with a clearly highlighted document TL;DR followed by a compact At a Glance table covering every named section, phase, PR, task, and collapsed resume section below it. Give every named section, phase, PR, and task a highlighted local TL;DR; a descriptive summary serves as the TL;DR for collapsed content. Keep prose to at most two short paragraphs per section; use bullets and tables for safety detail, placing resume-only paths, commands, assumptions, or handoff state in <details> blocks when useful. Preserve concrete migration safety: validation, rollout, rollback, dual-run ownership, and an explicit safe-cutover criterion. Show the human-readable layer before plan review; after direction approval, run plan-reviewer and resolve blocking scan-path and migration-safety findings before final approval.
evals.baseline_behavior: Earlier roadmaps contained sound implementation and safety detail but made readers discover the delivery sequence, rollout gates, and ownership boundaries by reading every section.
evals.eval_result: Codex iteration-3 fresh-context pass: 6/6 assertions after iteration 2's 5/6 exposed missing Phases and resume-detail rows. Automated checks also confirmed every heading has a local TL;DR and no section exceeds two prose paragraphs.
